question.leadin: This Northern Democrat opposed John C. Breckinridge for his party's presidential nomination in 1860.
question.text: Name this "Little Giant" from Illinois who defended popular sovereignty in his Freeport Doctrine.
question.clue: This man was famous for introducing the idea of "popular sovereignty" and was largely responsible for the Compromise of 1850. He engaged in a series of debates with the eventual winner of this election.

swap.text: The Battle of Hampton Roads took place between the USS Monitor and this confederate ship, also the name of the state where Hampton Roads is located.
swap.clue: The Confederates made this first ironclad, which sat largely underwater, from a captured frigate. It totally wrecked everything until it fought the Union ironclad Monitor inconclusively at Hampton Roads.

question.text: While Seward was being stabbed, Abraham Lincoln was being shot by this actor and Confederate sympathizer.
question.clue: Samuel Mudd created a splint for this man's broken leg.

swap.leadin: "If nominated I will not run; if elected I will not serve."
swap.text: Those words were spoken by this Ohioan, in reaction to suggestions that he should be the Republican nominee for president in 1884. He may be more notable for leading the March to the Sea after burning Atlanta.
swap.clue: After Lee's surrender at Appomattox Court House, this general met at Bennett Place to accept the surrender of Joseph Johnston.

question.leadin: He teamed up with Thaddeus Stevens as leaders of the Radical Republicans during Congressional Reconstruction.
question.text: Identify this Massachusetts Senator who argued against slavery in his "Crime Against Kansas" speech, and also attacked Stephen Douglas and Andrew Butler in anther speech denouncing the Kansas-Nebraska Act.
question.clue: This man had earlier described Stephen Douglass as the "Sancho Panza" to a man derided for his "incoherent phrases" and hoped that "South Carolina" would " howling."

swap.leadin: Name some American presidents who were also generals.
swap.text: This New Hampshire Democrat, Fillmore's successor, commanded a brigade in the Mexican-American War. He failed to control the sectionalism that led to the Civil War.
swap.clue: To gain land for the Southern Pacific Railroad, this man's Secretary of War arranged the Gadsden Purchase.

question.leadin: The Wisconsin Supreme Court's opinion that a component of this legislation was unconstitutional was overturned by the ruling in Ableman v. Booth.
question.text: Name this legislation that contained a component act ending the slave trade in Washington, D.C. Debates over this legislation featured Daniel Webster's "Seventh of March" speech and William Seward's "Higher Law" speech.
question.clue: The Seventh of March Speech byDaniel Webster supported this legislation, and one of its components upheld so-called "Bloodhound Laws."

swap.text: The Confederate forces at Shiloh were initially led by this general, whose death in the battle made him the highest ranking officer on either side to die in the war.
swap.clue: As a colonel, his forces took over for Edmund Alexander and successfully installed Alfred Cumming as governor during the Utah War, in which he camped at the burned-out Fort Bridger.

question.leadin: This action was led by Isaac Haight, John Lee, and other members of the Nauvoo Legion in conjunction with the Paiute tribe.
question.text: Identify this attack on the Baker-Fancher party which saw some very irate Mormons brutally execute its victims, and was possibly orchestrated by Brigham Young.
question.clue: During this event, a militia dressed up as Paiute ] Indians killed members of the Baker-Fancher wagon train.

swap.text: This politician succeeded Simon Cameron as Lincoln's Secretary of War. After Lincoln's assassination and a falling out with Johnson, this man refused to resign his office.
swap.clue: Lorenzo Thomas was selected to replace this man in one post during an ordeal that violated the Tenure of Office Act.

question.leadin: During this event, Lawrence Keitt brandished a gun and shouted "Let them be!"
question.text: Name this May 1856 event perpetrated by Preston Brooks in revenge for another man's offensive speech attacking Andrew Butler for Butler's support of the "harlot" slavery.
question.answerHtml: the caning of Charles Sumner [accept synonyms like assault instead of caning]
question.clue: Henry Edmundson and Laurence Keitt blocked onlookers to this event from intervening, and its perpetrator was fined only $300 by the District of Columbia.

swap.leadin: This photographer had earlier taken photos of former Presidents Andrew Jackson and John Quincy Adams.
swap.text: Name this Civil War photographer whose photos of Lincoln were used for the relief carved on the penny.
swap.clue: O'Sullivan was once employed by this way more famous photographer, who snapped Lincoln on the day of the Cooper Union speech. This man was almost captured taking photos at First Bull Run.

question.leadin: Note to players: two answers required. A law named for these two states broke a convention that declared slavery was banned north of the 36°30' ("thirty-six thirty") parallel.
question.text: Identify these two states that name an 1854 act that advocated for "popular sovereignty". The act led to one of these states's "Bleeding" period, which saw conflict between "jayhawkers" and "border ruffians".
question.answerHtml: Kansas and Nebraska [accept Kansas-Nebraska Act, prompt on partial answers, prompt on Bleeding Kansas]

swap.text: The last major action before the battle of Shiloh was Grant's capture of these two forts, one on the Tennessee River and one on the Cumberland.
swap.clue: Grant earned the nickname "Unconditional Surrender" after forcing John Floyd, Simon Bolivar Buckner, and Gideon Pillow to give up this Tennessee fort.

question.leadin: As a captain during the Mexican-American War, this man led the Ninety Six Guards of the Palmetto Regiment.
question.text: Name this politician who was angered by a speech that he saw as "a libel on South Carolina" and his cousin Andrew Butler.
question.clue: This senator from South Carolina famously attacked the author of the "The Crime Against Kansas" speech with a cane.

swap.text: In his Valley campaign of 1862, this general defeated three Union armies. He was killed by friendly fire at the Battle of Chancellorsville a year later and acquired his nickname at the First Battle of Bull Run.
swap.clue: His lateness at Mechanicsville and sluggishness at Gaines' Mill and White Oak swamp led to historical debate about the cause of his poor performance at the Seven Days, with most attributing it to fatigue from the march from the Shenandoah Valley Campaign.

question.leadin: Answer the following about women writing around the time of the Civil War.
question.text: This woman, a prominent Charleston socialite whose husband was an aide to Jefferson Davis, wrote an extensive diary of the Civil War, published posthumously by her friend Isabella Martin under the 1905 title A Diary from Dixie.
question.clue: This woman claimed that White women knew of other enslavers' children, but acted as if biracial children on their own estates "dropped from the clouds." C. Vann Woodward's annotated version of this woman's diary of the Civil War won a Pulitzer Prize.

swap.leadin: The V Corps of General Fitz-John Porter suffered heavy losses during one of these engagements.
swap.text: Identify these series of engagements that included the battles of Savage's Station and Frayser's Farm.
swap.clue: Including conflicts at Oak Grove and Malvern Hill, this series of conflicts near Richmond between McClellan and Lee marked the end of the Union general's Peninsula Campaign.

question.leadin: In his later life he was offered control of the armies of Romanian and Egypt but he decided it would be better to try to reform the New Orleans Lottery and to argue for the voting rights of slaves.
question.text: Identify this general who commanded men fighting Robert Anderson in an 1861 battle. His forces at a later battle won against the Union when he was commanding the Confederate troops with Joseph Johnston at Manassas.
question.clue: This Acadian confederate commander who was in charge of Charleston's defenses the night Fort Sumter was attacked.

swap.leadin: This man served as the president of the Union Pacific from 1863 to 1868.
swap.text: Name this New York governor who, at the beginning of the Civil War, arrested the Maryland legislature. He was appointed Secretary of the Treasury late in Buchanan term.
swap.clue: This man was elected in 1872 after working as minister to France and as Lincoln's Treasury Secretary, in which role he ordered that anyone taking down a Union flag in New Orleans was to be shot.
